**Check-runs on `e63f6ec2`, read once at 2026-10-27T03:12Z** (44 runs): no failure. Completed success, the ones that carry this PR's derived gates — `Type Check · source gates` (the token ratchet and its `--self-test`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs`; lint.yml L5358/L5490/L5618–5622) at 2026-10-27T03:11Z; `Lint · docs & code guards` (`check:role-word`, lint.yml L2326) at 2026-10-27T03:11Z; `Lint · ESLint`; `Lint · repo & tooling gates`; `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`; `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`; `Type Check · debt ledger`; `Build Core` (hosts `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, ci.yml L3069 — the reading the dev could not take locally) at 2026-10-27T03:08Z; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (twice); `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`; `No other open PR may claim the same issue`; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`; `Part-of PR must not also close its card`; `Check Changeset`; `Check PR Size`; `Dogfood Regression Gate`; `Plan Test Core shards`; `Test Core (3/8)`; `Auto Label`; `filter`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the merge queue waits on them, this record does not re-run them.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Every new sentence against the spec on `origin/main` — right, with four omissions named (none a falsehood).**

- `rules/security.md` "Membership keys" (L119–163 on the head). Declared on the roster object whose rows define the set, read with `in` from a permission set's policy — right: `object.zod.ts` L3199 (`membershipKeys: MembershipKeysSchema`, its describe) and `rls.zod.ts` L46–52 use case 6 and L54–69 "Where a membership key comes from". The example (`account_member`, `membershipKeys.portal_account_ids: { userField: 'user', valueField: 'account', filter: 'active == true' }`, policy `account in current_user.portal_account_ids`) is the spec's own shape (`portal_supplier_ids` with the same three members and the same `filter`). The three members: `userField` a single-valued user reference (`rls.zod.ts` L856–860; the spec also admits a `master_detail` to `sys_user` — the skill names `user` or a `lookup`, an omission); `valueField` a reference column, never the same column as `userField` (`superRefine` L889–897) — right; `filter` canonical CEL over the roster's own columns in the lowerable subset, reading no `current_user.*` (L872–876) — right. The refusals: one key on two objects refused by `defineStack` / `composeStacks` (`object.zod.ts` L3196–3197, `rls.zod.ts` L765–767) — right; the kernel names refused are exactly `RESERVED_RLS_MEMBERSHIP_KEYS` = `id`, `organization_id`, `positions`, `org_user_ids`, `accessible_org_ids`, `email` (`contracts/rls-membership-resolver.ts` L89–96) — the skill's list matches it one for one; contribution through an object extension refused (`object.zod.ts` L4256–4259) — right. The read: once per request, as a system read inside the caller's organization, no read on the roster needed, at most 1,000 values (`MEMBERSHIP_KEY_MAX_VALUES`, `rls.zod.ts` L798), and a larger set, a failed read or a `filter` that does not compile makes every policy reading it match no rows; whoever can write the roster's rows grants the key — every clause is in the key's describe (`object.zod.ts` L3199–3212). Omitted: a key a registered membership resolver also owns resolves from neither source (describe, `rls.zod.ts` L66–67) — an omission the one-line budget can carry later, not a falsehood. The choice rule (person → owner scoping; position → `positions` on the policy; named record → a membership key; one record once → a sharing rule or a manual share) is a judgment line consistent with the RLS policy's `positions` key and the `rls.zod.ts` use cases; nothing in it contradicts the spec.
- `rules/security.md` "Positions grant only what they name; portal users are `external`" (L166–180). A position distributes only the sets its `permissionSets` names, cited to ADR-0131 D3/D4 — right: `identity/position.zod.ts` L106–108 (`permissionSets: z.array(SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema).optional()`, describe "ADR-0131 D3/D4: the permission sets this position distributes, by name"), ADR-0131 D3 ("the position → permission-set binding is part of the position's definition"), and `name` / `label` are the schema's keys (L82, L85), so the one-line shape parses. "A set that merely shares the position's name is reported, never granted; a name matching no set confers nothing" — right: commit `733b3c849a` (#26064, `fix(plugin-security)!: retire the position-name fold; a namesake set is reported, never granted`) and `membership-role.ts` ("with no position of that name declaring `permissionSets` that name resolves to nothing"). The `external` tier: a closed list of five, one per member — right (`BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLES`, the "exclusive" bullet of `MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_EXTERNAL`; the docs anchor `#membership-tiers-are-a-closed-list` exists as a heading at `authentication.mdx` L836 and says the same five values); the `everyone` baseline (`isDefault` sets) does not reach it — right (`builtin-positions.ts` L63–68: projects to `org_external`, does NOT hold `everyone`, none of the deployment's defaults reach it); sees no member directory, holds no business unit — right (`membership-role.ts`, the directory doors answer its own membership only; "outside the department tree"); "every org-wide default is owner-only for it" — right, and the one clause I expected to be loose: `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` L854–857, "plugin-sharing floors an external principal's org-wide default at owner_only unless a held grant's RLS speaks for this object"; rows reach it only through explicit grants (a position or set whose row policies bound them, a sharing rule, a manual share) — right (`membership-role.ts`: "Data comes only through explicit grants: positions, permission sets and sharing"). The vocabulary: the schema's constant file says "membership role" (better-auth's own column, ADR-0090 D3's one exception); the hand-written docs page the skill links says "membership tier"; the skill teaches the docs page's word, the new prose carries no whole-word "role" (read L119–200), and `check:role-word` is green on the head (`Lint · docs & code guards`). The sentence taught is what the schema states; the gate's vocabulary is respected.
- `rules/relationships.md` "Owner edits under `controlled_by_parent` — `ownerMayEdit`" (L95–110) and the type-table Sharing cell (L16). Inherits the master's access; every write needs edit on the master; the opt-in lets the row's owner (`owner_id`) update that row by id with read access to the master; insert, delete, predicate (`multi: true`) updates and on-behalf-of writes still need master edit; the detail's own row policies still AND in — every clause is `object.zod.ts` L3073–3085 and L3114–3119 and ADR-0055 §3 as amended (#25760, ruling 6398566164). Refused at parse under any other `sharingModel` "(the owner already writes there)" — right, and the parenthesis is the refusal's own reason (`refuseControlledByParentOwnerMayEditOffDetail`, L2278–2286); refused one level up as `sharing.ownerMayEdit` — right (the spec test L95–100: `unrecognized_keys` at `sharing`, naming `sharing.controlledByParent`). Omitted: on an object with no `owner_id` column (`ownership: 'business_unit' | 'org' | 'none'`) the opt-in resolves inert and is reported once (ADR-0055 amendment, fail-closed boundaries) — an omission, not a falsehood.
- `references/seeds.md` `columns` row (L53) and "Columns the app owns after the first load" (L69–87). Replay on every dev-server boot and re-publish; `upsert` re-asserts every column on the matched row; `applyOn: 'create'` writes on create and leaves the row's value on every replay; an `update` dataset never writes it; `insert` / `ignore` / `replace` never update a matched row so nothing changes there; each key must be a field of the object or an injected system column, `defineSeed` refuses one that is not; same values and meaning as the import mapping entry's `applyOn` — every clause is `seed.zod.ts` L40–68 and L173–196 (one `ColumnApplyOnSchema`, `column-apply-on.zod.ts` L16–17), and the cross-link to objectstack-api (#26392) is a link, not a restatement. Omitted: a column of the dataset's `externalId` stays in the matched row's update whatever it declares (L52–54) — omission.
- `references/examples-objects.md` L42, L88: `{ type: 'lookup', reference: 'user' }` → `{ type: 'user' }`. Right: a `user` field's target is fixed to `sys_user` (`field-value.zod.ts` L180, `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS`) and a `reference` naming any other object is refused at the field's own door (`field.zod.ts` L2449–2483, `USER_FIELD_TARGET`); `user` was already the type the package teaches (`field-types.md` L98, `SKILL.md` L311). The body's sentence "a `user` field's target is fixed to `sys_user` and a foreign `reference` is refused" is true as written. Both blocks stay `os:check`-marked; their type-check reading is the pending `Type Check · consumer gates` run (the dev's local run: 265 pass).

**(b) Nothing removed beyond the stale lines the card names; nothing to cut under ruling A.** The diff's only deletions are the two `reference: 'user'` spellings the card names (examples-objects.md −2) and the one table cell rewritten with the opt-in added (relationships.md L16); every other hunk is additive. Ruling A's first step (削重复, cut genuine restatements in the same file first) — I read each touched file on `c51aed4f` for a restatement of each new clause, as the brief asked, rather than taking the dev's sentence-level scan: `security.md` L112 (the RLS table's `current_user.KEY` row) names the placeholder and where it comes from in one cell, which the new section's heading echoes in five words — not a restatement to cut, the row is the table's pointer to the section; `security.md` L30 (`isDefault: true` = the `everyone` baseline) is cross-referenced by the new parenthetical, not restated; `relationships.md` L16 and `SKILL.md` L76 name `controlled_by_parent` in a cell without the opt-in; `seeds.md` had no replay sentence (only "Idempotent re-runs" in the best-practice table, L160); `field-types.md` L98 / `SKILL.md` L311 teach the `user` type and are untouched. The neighbouring `when` section (#26393, security.md L182–209 on the head) is not restated. No genuine same-file duplicate exists to fund the additions; the dev's "nothing to cut, no surviving-home list" holds.

**(c) Ratchet rows pinned at the measurement; the ruling quoted where the script requires.** The measure is `Math.ceil(Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8') / 4)`, a pure function of the blob (script header L44–118; the stamp-line exclusion applies to `SKILL.md` only, untouched). Recomputed from `git show e63f6ec2:PATH | wc -c`: `rules/security.md` 14771 B → 3693 (row 3693 ✓; base 11821 B → 2956 under 2956, +737 at headroom 0); `rules/relationships.md` 15491 B → 3873 (row 3873 ✓; base 14687 B → 3672 measured under a 3676 ceiling — the body's "3672 → 3873" is the measurement and the thread's 3676 the old ceiling, both right: +201 measured, 4 absorbed, ceiling +197); `references/seeds.md` 6262 B → 1566 (row 1566 ✓; base 5194 B → 1299 under 1299, +267); `references/examples-objects.md` 7073 B → 1769 (row 1769 ✓; base 7115 B → 1779 under 1779, −10 — lowered to exactly the measurement, the one lowered row); `evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json` 5616 B → 1404 (row 1404 ✓; base 4377 B → 1095 under 1095, +309); `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` 4198 B → 1050 (row 1050 ✓; base 3782 B → 946 under 946, +104). Six rows, zero headroom each, no headroom smuggled in and no red gate; the arithmetic closes: measured +737 +201 +267 −10 +309 +104 = +1608, less the 4 tokens of headroom the relationships row absorbed = +1604 on the ceilings (+737 +197 +267 −10 +309 +104), and each per-row figure the body states matches the blob. The raise rule (header L127–129) requires a PR whose body quotes a maintainer ruling; the body quotes the tap verbatim (「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」, the card 「skills 修复卡的教学和 eval 都撞 token 天花板,怎么付?」, 2026-10-27T01:21Z) and so does each of the five raised rows' comments; the lowered row's comment says RE-LOCK with the net cut. The script's `--self-test` reads neither row comments nor the body (its "raise is bound to a quoted maintainer ruling" case checks the gate's own over-ceiling message), and its SKILL.md-subtotal pin (L1461–1464) moves only with a SKILL.md row — none moves here; both ran green in `Type Check · source gates`. Row-comment line length: no `max-len` rule in the eslint config on `origin/main`, and `Lint · ESLint` is green on the head. Lines, recomputed: security.md 249 → 312, relationships.md 401 → 418, seeds.md 142 → 163, examples-objects.md 197 → 197, hooks eval 55 → 65, objects eval 45 → 45; whole package (`SKILL.md` + `references/**/*.md` + `rules/**/*.md`, 14 files) 3736 → 3837 lines and 39497 → 40692 tokens as the sum of per-file `ceil(bytes/4)` over raw file bytes — the body's table, both readings, is exact. **Merge-base reconcile:** `git log c51aed4f..origin/main -- scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs skills/objectstack-data` = `591a796a` (#26385, ui rows) and `5507225e` (#26388, i18n eval row) — the only two sibling commits above the base on this tip; #26392 (`a66c9ff4`) and #26393 (`7c70f91c`) are below `c51aed4f`, and #26390 / #26407 are not on `origin/main` at `5507225e`. Both later commits edit other packages' rows; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main e63f6ec2` merges clean (exit 0, no conflict), and the six `objectstack-data` rows read identically on `origin/main` and on `c51aed4f` (2956 / 3676 / 1299 / 1779 / 1095 / 946) — no sibling row this PR carries is stale, no textual conflict for the queue.

**(d) Evals.** Both files parse as JSON on the head; ids 1–6 (hooks) and 1–4 (objects) unique and sequential. Over every case of both files, each `must_contain` string occurs in its `expected_output` and no `must_not_contain` string does (checked by script over the head blobs, all ten cases). The card-specific acceptance eval is hooks eval 6 ("Customers' staff … may read only the orders of the accounts they belong to"; expects `membershipKeys`, `current_user.portal_account_ids`, `userField`, `valueField`, `permissionSets`, `external`) — present and in the file's existing shape. Every new teaching has an eval: membership keys and the `external` tier and the position binding (hooks 6), `applyOn: 'create'` (hooks 4, prompt extended with the job-advanced `stage`), `ownerMayEdit` and `type: 'user'` with `must_not_contain: "reference: 'user'"` (objects 2, prompt extended with the owner-who-only-reads case). One precision note, not a defect: hooks 6's `must_not_contain: ["permissions: {"]` is described by the body as pinning "the object-level `permissions:` key"; `ObjectSchema` has no `permissions` key and the stack root takes an array (`permissions: [set]`, security.md L20), so the pinned spelling is wrong on either reading and the assertion is sound, but its rationale is not the one written. `evals/README.md` (headroom 1) does not name the new topics — observation, as the body says.

**(e) Wanted lines met, nothing beyond.** D2 `membershipKeys` with `userField` / `valueField` / `filter` and the choice against positions and a sharing rule → security.md ✓; D5 a position grants only what `permissionSets` names → security.md ✓; D6 `external` for portal users → security.md ✓; D3 `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit` → relationships.md ✓ (the card's own row at L16 and the new subsection); D4 `columns.FIELD.applyOn: 'create'` → seeds.md ✓; D7 `type: 'user'` at L42 and L88 → ✓. `SKILL.md` untouched (line 1 is PR #25640's; L48 and L76 do not point at the new sections — the body's Acceptance note says so; a pointer would need a SKILL.md row raise under ruling A). The seven changed paths are the claim's surface exactly: the six package files plus the ratchet script's `objectstack-data` rows and their comments, nothing else in the script. The field-permission `when` (#26179, landed as #26393) is not restated.

**(f) PR body dogfoods the current shape.** Line 1 the harness attribution HTML comment, line 2 the `_Requested by_` line, line 3 `Fixes #26297`, then `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial — os-dev.md L323 is the exemption in its own words (the harness-written attribution comment on line 1 stays as is, only reported; `Fixes #N` follows immediately), and the two closing-keyword guards (`The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`) are green on the head. No `Skills-docs:` line — right: pm-dispatch `SKILL.md` L313 owes it only for a kind other than `none` or a `(narrowing)` arm; the triage line's "updated here" (6431843467) predates the order and, had the line been written, it would have been true (teaches in `skills/**` and the evals exercise it). `## 维护者速读` six labels in order; 需要你做的 names one action (approve, or Merge when ready — right for Tier H); 先看 three files naming the risky hunks; 两分钟验证 one command with the expected sight, and the sight is what the script prints (`PATH is N tokens (ceiling N; headroom 0).` per file, `✓ check-skills-token-ratchet: N authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings; …` as the last line — script L969, L1057). English sections What changes / Why / Tests / Acceptance notes / Verification with the readings folded; the two-readings table recomputed exact in (c). No model name in the title, the body, the commit message or its trailers (`Claude-Session` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`, the model-free pair). `Removed:` names the two stale spellings only.

**(g) Report shape and claim.** os-dev-report 6432762671 (2026-10-27T03:08Z) carries every key of the os-dev.md JSON template on `origin/main` (issue, status, branch, pr, session, premise_still_valid, summary, tests, gates, dogfood_battery, mcp_calls, api_writes, open_questions, out_of_scope_findings) plus `deviations` (5) and `line_budget` as the order asked; `files_changed` / `rules_retired` are not keys of that template and are absent — consistent. Branch `claude/project-thread-un9ezo` = the claim's `Branch:` (6432432559); `mcp_calls: 4` (three GitHub reads, one platform read; no write), `api_writes: 2` (relay `pr_create`, the report comment). One sentence of the summary was stale a minute after it was written — "the PR stays a draft; nothing readied, armed or enqueued" is true of the dev's own acts, but os-zhuang's APPROVED review at 2026-10-27T03:07Z preceded the report, and the readying and arming are the approver's acts (named under ③).

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `skills/objectstack-data` carries no `package.json` (its tree is `SKILL.md`, `evals/`, `references/`, `rules/`), no `skills/**` path has one, and `scripts/**` publishes nothing; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. `Clause-②: no` (no contract changes — every key taught exists on `origin/main`) and `Metadata-protocol: none` (nothing a metadata author can write changes) are line-initial and true; no `Skills-docs:` line owed, as in ①(f).

1. **Landing-state deviation from the Tier H sequence** (not the dev's act): the order said draft until the contract review and the maintainer's hand or an authorized APPROVED review; os-zhuang (a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` account) approved, readied and armed auto-merge at 2026-10-27T03:07Z, before any review record existed. The review is now on record for this head; the queue guard reads it in the merge group.

3. **Process:** the harness's "add os-warren as reviewer" was not done through MCP (correct under the ban); the relay requested hotlong and os-zhuang at `pr_create`; os-zhuang has reviewed.
4. **Process:** `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT-MEASURED locally (whole-repo build prerequisite); its CI reading is `Build Core` success at 2026-10-27T03:08Z. The worktree `objectstack-issue-26297` is retained for a rework round and is cleaned after this verdict.

Hand-written docs, not a skills card. Dedupe words: `rls.mdx membershipKeys context variables`, `current_user.KEY docs`.
6. **Precision to-dos, not defects (each an omission, carried in a later line when a row has headroom):** (i) `SKILL.md` L48 does not name membership keys and L76 does not point at `ownerMayEdit` — a pointer costs a SKILL.md row raise under ruling A; (ii) `userField` also admits a `master_detail` to `sys_user`; (iii) the `ownerMayEdit` opt-in is inert and reported on an object without an `owner_id` column; (iv) a column of the seed's `externalId` stays in the matched row's update whatever `applyOn` it declares; (v) a key a registered membership resolver also owns resolves from neither source; (vi) the stated rationale of hooks eval 6's `must_not_contain: "permissions: {"`; (vii) `evals/README.md` does not name the new topics (headroom 1).
